title: Campaign Map
description: The raster campaign map's manifest -- the singleton that makes a pixel on the picture mean a place on the ground. The map itself is a hand-finished Photoshop file (the vector renderer that produced its base is retired), so nothing regenerates these numbers: they are the standing contract between the image, the reference grid, and the map frame it was exported from. Consumed by tools/gazetteer/core/georef.py. The image it points at lives under artwork/, which is gitignored -- this tracked file is the only durable record of what that image is and how to read it, the same arrangement asset-registry.json already uses.

image.description: The master raster. `path` is repo-relative and may point into a gitignored tree.

sha256.description: Hash of the master as last calibrated. A mismatch means the map has been re-exported and the tile pyramid, and possibly the calibration, are stale. Null only if never hashed.

border.description: The painted margin around the content area. Page furniture -- grid ticks and labels live here. Not part of the mapped ground.

content.description: The mapped ground, inside the margin. Must be square: it is the map frame's page square.

grid.description: The reference grid. Two-tier: major squares of `cellsPerMajor` cells, lettered by column and numbered by row, then the cell's position inside its major as two digits. See tools/gazetteer/core/grid.py.

frameRef.description: Id of the map frame in data/map/frames/ that this raster was exported from. It supplies the centre, the page rotation, the extent and the CRS -- everything needed to turn a content pixel into lon/lat.

metresPerPixel.description: Ground metres per content pixel. Derived from the frame (extentM / content width) and asserted against it on load, so a wrong value fails rather than silently rescaling the world. Null to skip the assertion.

calibration.description: Whether the Photoshop master still registers on the frame's page square. `exact` means it does and no correction is applied. `affine` means it drifted (a crop or a resample between export and hand-finishing) and the six coefficients correct raw content pixels before they are projected.

matrix.description: [a, b, c, d, e, f] for x' = a*x + b*y + c, y' = d*x + e*y + f. Required when mode is affine.

residualPx.description: Worst control-point residual at the last calibration, in pixels. 1 px is 1 m here, so this is also the map's positional accuracy in metres.

controlPoints.description: Identifiable features used to check registration, each an image pixel paired with the real lon/lat it should land on. Kept so the check is repeatable rather than a one-off eyeball.

tiles.description: The pyramid the annotation UI pans over, built from the master by tools/gazetteer/tile.py. Null before it has been built.
